sobre.description: About us: Thr33 Labs is an independent interactive technology studio, incorporated in 2026, with its registered office in Óbidos, Portugal.

head.label: About
head.h1: An interactive technology studio in Óbidos
head.lead: Thr33 Labs is the brand of THR33XYZ LABS - TECNOLOGIA E CONSULTORIA, UNIPESSOAL LDA, a company incorporated in 2026 with its registered office in Óbidos, Portugal.

paragraphs: We are an independent interactive technology studio. We bring together hardware, software and augmented reality to create apps, platforms and interactive experiences, such as games for events.
When a project calls for it, we bring in trusted partners in design, development and augmented reality, always with a single point of contact at Thr33 Labs.
Besides client work, we build our own products, such as Vizia, an augmented reality product.
Founded by Thiago Oliveira, Software Engineer with over 10 years of experience.

privacidade.title: Privacy policy · Thr33 Labs
privacidade.description: How Thr33 Labs handles personal data on thr33.xyz and in email and phone contacts, under the GDPR.

head.label: GDPR
head.lead: The thr33.xyz website has no forms and no advertising. It uses Google Analytics to measure visits, only if you accept analytics cookies. This page explains what data we handle and why.

blocks.p: THR33XYZ LABS - TECNOLOGIA E CONSULTORIA, UNIPESSOAL LDA, tax number (NIPC) 519573021, registered office at Beco da Serra, 2, Sobral da Lagoa, 2510-651 Óbidos, Portugal. Privacy contact: hello@thr33.xyz, with the subject "Privacy".

ul: Website visits. Like any website, the server logs technical requests: IP address, date and time, requested page, browser and operating system. We do not use this data to identify visitors or build profiles.

Visit statistics. If you accept analytics cookies, Google Analytics collects usage data: pages viewed, visit duration, where you came from, device type and approximate location. Google Analytics 4 does not store IP addresses.
Email or phone contacts. If you contact us, we handle your name, email address or phone number, your company and the content of your message.
Clients. If we start a project together, we handle the data needed for the contract and invoicing.
Keeping the website available and secure, and detecting abuse: legitimate interest (Article 6(1)(f) GDPR).
Measuring how the website is used, to improve it: consent (Article 6(1)(a)), which you can withdraw at any time under "Cookie settings" in the footer.
Answering enquiries and preparing proposals: steps taken at your request before a contract (Article 6(1)(b)).
Performing client contracts: performance of a contract (Article 6(1)(b)).
Meeting tax and accounting obligations: legal obligation (Article 6(1)(c)).

blocks.p: We do not sell personal data or use it for advertising or automated decision-making.
We use service providers that process data on our behalf, under contracts that require them to protect it:

ul: Hetzner Online (Germany): website hosting.

Cloudflare: content delivery and protection against attacks. It may process data outside the European Union, under the EU-US Data Privacy Framework and the European Commission's standard contractual clauses.
Zoho (European Union data centre): email.
Google Ireland Limited (Ireland): Google Analytics, only with your consent. It may process data in the United States, under the EU-US Data Privacy Framework.
Certified accountant: client invoicing data.

blocks.p: The website's fonts are served by the website itself. The only third-party request is Google Analytics, and only after you accept.

ul: Server technical logs: up to 30 days.
Google Analytics data: 14 months.
Enquiries that do not lead to a project: up to 2 years after the last contact.
Client and invoicing data: for the duration of the contract and then for the legal periods (10 years for tax documents).

blocks.p: You can ask to access, correct, erase, restrict or port your data, and object to processing based on legitimate interest. Send your request to hello@thr33.xyz. We reply within one month.
You can also complain to the Portuguese data protection authority, Comissão Nacional de Proteção de Dados (cnpd.pt).
The website sets one cookie to remember your choice and, only if you accept, Google Analytics cookies. The details are in the cookie policy.
The website links to other services, such as Vizia and Get It Vac, which have their own privacy policies.
If this policy changes, we publish the new version here with its update date.

cookies.title: Cookie policy · Thr33 Labs
cookies.description: Which cookies thr33.xyz uses, what for, and how to accept or reject Google Analytics cookies.

head.label: Cookies
head.lead: The thr33.xyz website sets one cookie to remember your choice and, only if you accept, Google Analytics cookies to measure visits.

blocks.p: Cookies are small files a website stores in your browser. Some are needed for the website to work. Others, such as analytics cookies, can only be used with your consent.

ul: thr33_consent (Thr33 Labs, necessary): remembers whether you accepted or rejected analytics cookies. Lasts 6 months.
_ga (Google Analytics, analytics): tells visits apart under a pseudonym. Lasts 2 years. Only with consent.
_ga_<ID> (Google Analytics, analytics): keeps the session state. Lasts 2 years. Only with consent.
__cf_bm (Cloudflare, necessary): may be set to protect the website against bots. Lasts 30 minutes.

blocks.p: Google Analytics is a service of Google Ireland Limited, Gordon House, Barrow Street, Dublin 4, Ireland. We use it to see which pages are viewed and how people reach the website, in aggregate numbers. We do not use it for advertising or profiling, and advertising signals are turned off.
Data may be processed in the United States, under the EU-US Data Privacy Framework. More information in Google's privacy policy.

blocks.h2: Accept, reject or change your mind

blocks.p: On your first visit, a notice asks whether you accept analytics cookies. Rejecting is as easy as accepting, and the website works the same either way. Until you choose, Google Analytics is not loaded.

You can change your choice at any time under "Cookie settings" in the footer of every page, or delete cookies in your browser settings. If you reject after accepting, we delete the Google Analytics cookies.
To see how we handle personal data, read the privacy policy. Questions: hello@thr33.xyz.

get-it-vac.title: Get It Vac · Case study · Thr33 Labs
get-it-vac.description: A Thr33 Labs case study: an arcade game controlled by an internet-connected mini robot vacuum, with multiplayer, AR and anonymous data, built in 5 days.
get-it-vac.og_image_alt: Get It Vac, a case study by Thr33 Labs, interactive technology studio

items.text: Projects

head.eyebrow: Caso de estudo · Web Summit Lisboa 2026 (unofficial stand)
head.lead: An arcade game controlled by an internet-connected mini robot vacuum, with phone multiplayer, photos, augmented reality and anonymous data. We built it in 5 days.

image.name: get-it-vac/hero
image.alt: Illustration of the Get It Vac screen: the mini robot vacuum on a pixel art race through Lisbon's neighbourhoods.

sections.label: Challenge
items: Bring hardware, web and augmented reality together in a single flow, with low latency between the robot and the screen.
Measure use without personal data: no cookies, no email, no accounts and no IP addresses.
Do it all in 5 days, from the first sketch to the game going live.

items.title: The game
items.text: A 400 m race through Lisbon's neighbourhoods, in pixel art drawn on canvas.

items.title: The controller
items.text: Microcontrollers and a joystick inside the robot vacuum, connected over Wi-Fi to a WebSocket relay that passes each move to the game.

images.name: get-it-vac/comando
images.alt: Illustration of the controller: the mini robot vacuum opened up, with the microcontrollers and the joystick that control the game.

items.title: Multiplayer
items.text: Up to 5 phones play at the same time. Each person joins with a QR code, with no app and no account.

images.name: get-it-vac/multijogador
images.alt: Illustration of multiplayer: three phones playing Get It Vac, next to the QR code to join.

items.title: Phone version
items.text: A selfie with a tile frame to share, and augmented reality on the game poster.

images.name: get-it-vac/selfie
images.alt: Illustration of the selfie: a navigator with the blue and white tile frame from the phone version.

images.name: get-it-vac/cartaz-ar
images.alt: Illustration of the AR poster: a phone pointed at the Get It Vac poster, with the robot in augmented reality on top.

items.title: Anonymous data dashboard
items.text: A dashboard with sessions, races and multiplayer rounds, with no cookies and no personal data.

sections.label: Results

items.term: races played in groups on the event day

sections.note: Multiplayer kept people playing. We measured everything with no cookies and no personal data.

sections.label: Learnings
items: Multiplayer is what keeps people playing.
The start of the game needs to be easier.
Hardware on event networks needs its own network and a plan B.
Building in privacy from the start did not stop us from getting useful data.

sections.text: We build custom games for events, activations and campaigns. Tell us the idea and the timeline, and we will reply with next steps.
